title: 02 Trigonometry: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Wrap Then Project | an angle dragged around the unit circle, with the terminal point, its two coordinates, the exact values at the sixteen special angles, the running cos^2 + sin^2 check and a count of how many angles share the same sine | the terminal point IS (cos, sin) in that order and the quadrant only fixes signs, the Pythagorean identity is just x^2 + y^2 = 1 renamed, and because many angles share one sine the wrap has no inverse until it is restricted

2. Adding Two Angles | two angle sliders composing one rotation, with the identity expanded term by term against the direct value, the failed 'sin A + sin B' row, and a separate tangent calculator driven by tan A and tan B | rotating by B then A is one rotation by A + B, which is where the identities and the minus sign in cos(A+B) come from, while tan(A+B) = (tanA+tanB)/(1-tanA tanB) goes undefined exactly when the angles sum to 90 degrees

3. One Branch Only | sin, cos or tan drawn across several periods with the kept branch shaded, a draggable horizontal line counting crossings, and a round-trip slider comparing arcf(f(theta)) with theta | an inverse exists only after the domain is cut to one monotone branch, so arcsin returns an angle in [-pi/2, pi/2] and arcsin(sin theta) gives theta back only when theta was already inside it

4. Any Triangle Now | the five data shapes SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS and SSA, each solving and drawing the triangle to scale from one draggable quantity, with the altitude h = b sin(A) governing the SSA case | the shape of the given data selects the law (SAS and SSS to the Law of Cosines, ASA, AAS and SSA to the Law of Sines), the Law of Cosines is Pythagoras plus -2ab cos(C), and only SSA can produce two valid triangles

5. Fit And Solve Waves | amplitude, B, shift and midline sliders over y = A sin(B(x - C)) + D with max, min and midline marked, plus a target line whose crossings are solved live | amplitude and midline are read from the extremes as (max - min)/2 and (max + min)/2, and solving needs the inverse for the principal angle plus the circle's mirror at pi minus it, with no solution at all once (k - D)/A exceeds 1
